entities.name: T1190
entities.evidence: The actors continue to breach organizations by exploiting web server vulnerabilities in public-facing devices and have conducted widespread activity against a number of different organizations simultaneously [T1190].

entities.name: T1059
entities.evidence: The authoring agencies assess the actors prefer netstat commands, such as netstat – naop and netstat – noa [T1059].

entities.name: T1027
entities.evidence: These files are typically multiple megabytes in size and often contain unusual file section names such as vmp0 and vmp1 for VMProtect and Themida or randomized file section names for Themida [T1027].

entities.name: T1003
entities.evidence: The authoring agencies assess the actors change settings on compromised systems to force the system to store credentials and then use the aforementioned tools to steal credentials. In one instance, the actors used the vssadmin command-line utility to back up a volume to retrieve a copy of the NTDS.dit file containing Active Directory data. In another instance, the actors were observed collecting registry hive data for offline extraction of credentials [T1003].

entities.name: T1087
entities.evidence: The tool is capable of receiving and executing command line arguments to enumerate directories and files and compress output files. The tool collects the following information for each drive targeted on a system: depth relative to starting path, name, last write time, last access time, creation time, size, and attributes [T1087, T1083].

entities.name: CVE-2021-44228
entities.evidence: The actors gain initial access through widespread exploitation of web servers through known vulnerabilities, such as CVE-2021-44228 (“Log4Shell”) in Apache’s Log4j software library and other CVEs listed above, to deploy web shells and gain access to sensitive information and applications for further exploitation.

entities.name: Enumerate directories and files using SMB
entities.evidence: The actors also enumerate directories and files of connected devices using Server Message Block (SMB) protocol...

entities.name: System logging for discovery
entities.evidence: The actors also use system logging for discovery to move laterally.

entities.name: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) for lateral movement
entities.evidence: The actors have also used Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) to move laterally.

entities.name: Tunneling over various protocols
entities.evidence: The actors leverage techniques and infrastructure positioned around the world to send commands to compromised systems.

entities.name: Tunneling tools for C2 operations
entities.evidence: They also use tunneling tools such as 3Proxy, PLINK, and Stunnel as well as custom proxy tunneling tools to tunnel traffic over a variety of protocols...

entities.name: Data collection using custom tools
entities.evidence: Malware previously used by the actors permitted placement and access to search through files that could be of interest...

entities.name: Data exfiltration to cloud storage
entities.evidence: The actors typically exfiltrate data to web services such as cloud storage or servers not associated with their primary C2.

entities.name: Data exfiltration using FTP and other protocols
entities.evidence: The actors have also been observed using the utilities PuTTY and WinSCP to exfiltrate data to North Korea-controlled servers via File Transfer Protocol (FTP) and other protocols.

entities.name: HTTP GET requests for information retrieval
entities.evidence: The actors have also been identified staging files for exfiltration on victim machines, establishing Remote Desktop Protocol connections, and conducting HTTP GET requests on port 80 to receive information.
